Dynamic model chill portions

Source: R/chill_portions.R
chill_portions.Rd

Accumulates chill portions (CP) with the Dynamic model of Fishman, Erez and Couvillon (1987a, b) as parameterised by Erez et al. (1990).

Usage

chill_portions(
  temperature,
  method = "dynamic",
  output = c("cumulative", "hourly", "total"),
  state = NULL,
  na_action = c("propagate", "hold"),
  e0 = 4153.5,
  e1 = 12888.8,
  a0 = 139500,
  a1 = 2.567e+18,
  slope = 1.6,
  tf = 277
)

Arguments

temperature

Numeric vector, or matrix with one row per series and one column per hour, of hourly temperatures (degrees Celsius) ordered in time.

method

Currently only "dynamic".

output

"cumulative" (default), "hourly" increments or "total".

state

Optional state returned by a previous call (attribute "state"), to continue the accumulation. NULL starts from zero.

na_action

"propagate" or "hold" (see Missing values).

e0, e1, a0, a1, slope, tf

Model constants.

Value

Chill portions with the shape implied by output, with attribute "state": a list with elements inter (intermediate at the start of the next hour) and portions (accumulated portions), one value per series.

Model

Chill accumulates in two steps. A thermally labile intermediate \(x\) forms in cool conditions and is destroyed by warm conditions. Once \(x \ge 1\), a temperature-dependent fraction \(\xi\) of it is fixed irreversibly as a chill portion. For each hour with temperature \(T_K = T + 273\) (K):

$$x_s = \frac{A_0}{A_1} e^{(E_1 - E_0)/T_K}, \qquad k_1 = A_1 e^{-E_1 / T_K}$$ $$\xi = \frac{s}{1 + s}, \qquad s = \exp\left(\frac{\mathrm{slope}\, T_f (T_K - T_f)}{T_K}\right)$$ $$x_h = x_s - (x_s - S_h) e^{-k_1}$$

where \(S_h\) is the intermediate at the start of the hour. If \(x_h \ge 1\), \(\Delta CP_h = \xi_h x_h\) and the next hour starts from \(S_{h+1} = x_h (1 - \xi_h)\); otherwise \(\Delta CP_h = 0\) and \(S_{h+1} = x_h\). The defaults are the published constants (E0 = 4153.5 K, E1 = 12888.8 K, A0 = 139500, A1 = 2.567e18, slope = 1.6, Tf = 277 K), identical to those of chillR::Dynamic_Model().

State and blocks

The intermediate is carried from hour to hour and day to day; the model is never reset implicitly (for example at month boundaries). The state after the last hour is returned in the "state" attribute. Passing it as state to a subsequent call continues the accumulation, so processing a season in blocks gives the same result as processing it at once. Define the accumulation period by subsetting temperature (see season_days()).

Indexing relative to chillR

thermify assigns the portion produced during hour \(h\) to hour \(h\). chillR::Dynamic_Model() reports the same quantity one position later (its first element is always zero and the contribution of the final hour is not included), so chillR cumulative output at position \(h + 1\) equals thermify cumulative output at position \(h\).

Missing values

With na_action = "propagate" (default) the state becomes NA from the first missing hour onwards, because the intermediate cannot be updated without temperature. na_action = "hold" keeps the intermediate unchanged and adds no portion during missing hours; this is a pragmatic gap-bridging assumption that should be reported, and the number of held hours is returned in the "n_missing" attribute. Gaps longer than a few hours should be filled with a defensible method before using the model.

References

Fishman, S., Erez, A., & Couvillon, G. A. (1987a). The temperature dependence of dormancy breaking in plants: computer simulation of processes studied under controlled temperatures. Journal of Theoretical Biology, 126(3), 309-321.

Fishman, S., Erez, A., & Couvillon, G. A. (1987b). The temperature dependence of dormancy breaking in plants: mathematical analysis of a two-step model involving a cooperative transition. Journal of Theoretical Biology, 124(4), 473-483.

Erez, A., Fishman, S., Linsley-Noakes, G. C., & Allan, P. (1990). The dynamic model for rest completion in peach buds. Acta Horticulturae, 276, 165-174.

Luedeling, E., Zhang, M., & Girvetz, E. H. (2009). Climatic changes lead to declining winter chill for fruit and nut trees in California during 1950-2099. PLoS ONE, 4(7), e6166.

See also

chill_units(), hourly_temperatures().

Examples

temp <- rep(c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4), length.out = 24 * 30)
cp <- chill_portions(temp)
tail(cp, 1)
#> [1] 23.01771

# Block processing gives the same answer
a <- chill_portions(temp[1:300])
b <- chill_portions(temp[301:720], state = attr(a, "state"))
all.equal(tail(as.vector(b), 1), tail(as.vector(cp), 1))
#> [1] TRUE
